summary: Barbara Mittler works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a Ph.D. from SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran 1 in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Barnard College, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch, she held professorships at Barnard College and Columbia University.

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and she held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Amsterdam from around 1894 to 1906 and later served there as a professor from 1907 to 1944.

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher, and held posts at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences, Heidelberg University, and Leiden University.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history/archaeology and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University, and held posts at the ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.
Barnabé Brisson studied at the College of Juilly, École polytechnique, and École des Ponts ParisTech, where he later held an academic post from 1820 to 1824.

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley and the Keck School of Medicine of USC, and he held posts at the University of Washington, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and The University of Hong Kong.
Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Charles Willemen and held a post as Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2019).
Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University. He later held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (around 1823–1831).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He held professorships in Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. at Stanford University, she held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor at Washington University in St. Louis.

Beatrice Erskine Lane worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, earned a master's at Columbia University, and was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology, studying at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held positions at Maryland, Heidelberg, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1905–1919) and Charles University (circa 1919–1952).
Beiho Takashima was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Toyo University and later held a post there.
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.
